issues.description: Email regex pattern is too permissive and allows many invalid email formats (e.g., 'a@b.c', 'user@.com')
issues.suggestion: Use a more comprehensive email validation regex following RFC 5322 or leverage a library like 'email-validator' for robust validation

issues.description: Multiple chained .replace() calls create intermediate string objects, reducing performance for large inputs
issues.suggestion: Use a single regex replacement with character mapping: return input.replace(/[<>"']/g, char => htmlEntities[char])

issues.description: ID generation uses Math.random() which is not cryptographically secure; may be predictable if IDs need security properties
issues.suggestion: Replace with crypto.randomUUID() or crypto.getRandomValues() for cryptographically secure ID generation

issues.description: Timestamp-based ID generation using Date.now() may produce collisions under high concurrency
issues.suggestion: Use a proper UUID library (uuid v4) or combine timestamp with a monotonic counter for guaranteed uniqueness

issues.description: Generic Error class used for multiple error conditions; lacks specific error type information
issues.suggestion: Create custom error classes like ValidationError, InvalidEmailError to enable better error handling and differentiation

issues.description: Database query execution line is commented out in production code, making the function incomplete
issues.suggestion: Either implement the database call or remove the commented code; if intentional, document why with a TODO comment

codeQuality.summary: This code exhibits solid security practices with input sanitization and parameterized queries, but has genuine technical concerns. Email validation is too permissive, ID generation lacks cryptographic security, and performance could be optimized in string handling. The commented database call should be either implemented or removed. The code falls short of the intended 85+ score for clean code due to security and validation concerns.

testCoverage.summary: The clean-code.ts fixture file has ZERO test coverage (0%). All functions are completely untested, including critical security functions (email validation, XSS sanitization) and the main business logic (createUser). Critical concerns: (1) Email validation regex may be insufficient, (2) XSS sanitization only applies to name field, not email, (3) No error handling for database failures, (4) ID generation uniqueness not verified, (5) No integration tests for full user creation flow. Estimated test implementation: 12-15 test suites covering 40+ individual test cases needed to reach 85%+ coverage.

suggestions.description: Use a more robust email validation approach. The current regex is overly simplistic and doesn't validate proper email format per RFC standards.
suggestions.benefits: Improved email validation accuracy, reduces false positives/negatives, follows RFC 5322 standards

suggestions.description: Consolidate multiple replace calls into a single operation using a more elegant approach with a character map
suggestions.benefits: More maintainable, easier to add new escape sequences, better performance for large strings, single regex pattern

suggestions.description: Extract validation logic into a separate validateUserInput function to improve separation of concerns and testability
suggestions.benefits: Improved code organization, easier to unit test validation separately, reduces complexity in createUser function, better separation of concerns

suggestions.description: Use crypto module for more robust ID generation. Current approach has potential collisions with high concurrency.
suggestions.benefits: Better cryptographic randomness, reduced collision risk, standard UUID format, more suitable for distributed systems

suggestions.description: Consider using readonly properties to make the interface immutable and prevent accidental mutations
suggestions.benefits: Enforces immutability at compile time, prevents accidental mutations, aligns with functional programming practices

suggestions.description: Create custom error classes for different validation scenarios instead of generic Error objects
suggestions.before:
throw new Error('Email and name are required');
throw new Error('Invalid email format');
suggestions.benefits: Better error handling and recovery, distinguishable error types, easier to implement proper error handling in calling code

suggestions.description: Add const assertions to query and params for improved type safety
suggestions.before:
const query = 'INSERT INTO users (id, email, name, created_at) VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4)';
const params = [user.id, user.email, user.name, user.createdAt];
suggestions.after:
const query = 'INSERT INTO users (id, email, name, created_at) VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4)' as const;
const params = [user.id, user.email, user.name, user.createdAt] as const;
suggestions.benefits: Improved type safety, enables better type inference, prevents accidental string mutations

refactorings.summary: The code demonstrates good foundational practices with proper input validation, XSS protection, and parameterized queries. Key modernization opportunities include: (1) replacing chained string replacements with a character map, (2) extracting validation logic into a dedicated function, (3) improving ID generation with crypto-secure methods, (4) implementing custom error classes, and (5) adding readonly properties. These changes enhance maintainability, testability, and robustness while following modern TypeScript best practices.

recommendations.description: Implement comprehensive test suite covering all functions with edge cases. Focus on security-critical functions (isValidEmail, sanitizeInput) and main business logic (createUser). Target 85%+ code coverage with mocked database interactions.

Replace Math.random() with crypto.randomUUID() or crypto.getRandomValues() for cryptographically secure ID generation. This is critical for production systems where ID predictability could be a security concern.
Improve email validation to support RFC 5322 standards or use a dedicated validation library. Current regex is too permissive and allows invalid email formats.
Refactor sanitizeInput() to use a single regex replacement with character mapping instead of chained .replace() calls. This improves performance for large input strings.
Extract validation logic from createUser() into a separate validateUserInput() function. This improves code organization, testability, and separates concerns.
Replace generic Error class with custom error classes (ValidationError, InvalidEmailError) to enable better error differentiation and handling in calling code.
Either implement the commented database query in saveUser() or remove it with documentation. Commented production code reduces maintainability.
